lines: Okay friend, here's the whole sermon in one box. Jesus flips what counts as blessed. He calls the poor, the hungry and the weeping blessed, and says "woe" to the rich, the well fed and the ones laughing now (Luke 6:20-26). What you've got NOW isn't the whole story, because "great is your reward in heaven" (Luke 6:23).

And the heart of it is the hardest thing in the recipe: love your enemies (Luke 6:27), give without keeping score (Luke 6:30), lend expecting nothing in return (Luke 6:35). Why? Because that's what God is like. "He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked" (Luke 6:35).

No scoreboard. No receipts. No "remember when I helped you move?" Just "Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful" (Luke 6:36). And the measure you use is the measure that comes back to you (Luke 6:38).

And before you go correcting anybody, check who's leading you and check your own eye. A student ends up like his teacher (Luke 6:40), and a blind guide just walks you both into a pit (Luke 6:39). So deal with your own BEAM first. Then you "will see clearly" enough to help your brother with his speck (Luke 6:42). Trust me, friend. I stamped crooked for YEARS. I am the LAST stamper who should be inspecting other people's cookies.

Here's what's underneath all of it: what comes out of you shows what's inside you. A tree is known by its fruit, and "out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks" (Luke 6:44-45). So it's not about looking good on the outside. It's about what's stored up in the heart, because that's what comes out (Luke 6:45).

So here's the big idea: hearing isn't enough, and calling Him "Lord, Lord" isn't enough. The one who hears His words and acts on them builds on the rock, and when the torrent hits, that house doesn't shake (Luke 6:46-49).
Reading the recipe and baking the recipe are two VERY different things. Ask anybody who's read the instructions twice and never once turned the oven on. Zero cookies, friend.
